seo.title: WorkStudio
seo.seo_title: Nexora WorkStudio: AI agents and workflows
seo.seo_description: Design, connect and run AI agents and workflows, with human approval, traces, evaluations and an OpenAI-compatible API. Demonstration on request.

translation.headline: Design, connect, run. In plain language.
translation.subheadline: Nexora WorkStudio brings the design, connection and running of agents and workflows into one place. A step can wait for a person's approval before acting.

blocks.role: Scénario type : de la demande à la trace, six temps.

translation.title: From request to trace.
translation.intro: A typical scenario, in six stages. Each stage is set up in WorkStudio, without writing code.

cards.title: 1. A request arrives.
cards.text: By email, by a form, by chat, on a schedule or through an API call.

cards.title: 2. Information is retrieved.
cards.text: The agent searches the document bases you authorized.

cards.title: 3. A proposal is prepared.
cards.text: A reply draft, a record, a pre-entry line, depending on the case.

cards.title: 4. An approval is requested.
cards.text: The workflow stops on a card showing the planned action. A person approves or refuses.

cards.title: 5. The action runs.
cards.text: Once, if it was authorized. Otherwise, nothing goes out.

cards.title: 6. Everything is traced.
cards.text: Who asked what, what was answered, with which model, in how much time.

blocks.role: Concevoir : agents, flux, Copilote, connaissances, documents et voix.

translation.title: Design your agents.
translation.intro: “Available” means delivered in the current version and verified on Nexora's test server. It does not mean a customer is already using it.

cards.title: Agents.
cards.text: A specialized assistant: it follows your instructions, uses the tools and documents you authorize, cites its sources and is published in a chat.

cards.title: Workflows.
cards.text: A sequence of steps, shown as cards or on a canvas (a drawing screen), tested step by step, then deployed through chat, schedule, event or an automatic call from another service. Every deployment is a version you can return to.

cards.title: A Copilot.
cards.text: Describe an automation in plain language: it prepares a workflow you review before creating it. Starter templates for small businesses (quotes, reminders, email sorting, meeting minutes) are provided.

cards.title: Knowledge.
cards.text: A base of your documents, indexed by default on the instance's server: agents answer from it with their sources.

cards.title: Documents read.
cards.text: Reading of scanned PDFs and images, extraction of fields from an invoice, quote, purchase order or expense report, with a “to verify” flag.

cards.title: Voice.
cards.text: Transcription of audio recordings, with a meeting's speakers, and reading a text aloud. No call-answering service is included.

blocks.role: Contrôler : validation, garde-fous, gouvernance, lieu des modèles.

cards.title: Human approval.
cards.text: Each action tool of an agent asks, by default, for a person's agreement before writing or deleting. With no answer, the action does not happen.

cards.title: Safeguards.
cards.text: Before going on, you can check that a format is valid, that personal information is absent or masked, or that an answer stays faithful to your knowledge. A safeguard reduces error; it does not eliminate it.

cards.title: Data policies.
cards.text: For each workspace: allow, mask or refuse sending personal information to a model outside the instance. Access groups can forbid certain models.

cards.title: Organizations and roles.
cards.text: Organizations, roles, an audit log and monthly consumption caps. Single sign-on with the usual identity providers.

cards.title: Each model's location.
cards.text: Every model shows whether it runs on your server, in Europe or at a third party. It is a documented display, not proof of residency.

blocks.role: Mesurer et améliorer : Playground, prompts, traces, évaluations, lots, consommation.

cards.title: A Playground.
cards.text: Try and compare several models side by side before choosing, with the time and tokens (the unit of text a model processes) of each answer.

cards.title: Versioned instructions.
cards.text: A reusable instruction has versions and two labels, production and test. You test a version before promoting it; every change is logged.

cards.title: Traces.
cards.text: Every model call leaves a trace: steps, duration, tokens, model. Personal information can be masked in them.

cards.title: Evaluations.
cards.text: Test sets and judges measure whether an agent, an instruction or a model answers well, and compare two versions before changing.

cards.title: Batch processing.
cards.text: Have a table of several hundred rows processed in the background: progress, cancellation, CSV export.

cards.title: Measured consumption.
cards.text: Tokens, runs and estimated carbon footprint, by model, workspace and person, with monthly caps.

blocks.role: Brancher : Nexora Connect, API, site, Assistant, délégation, installation.

cards.title: Connectors.
cards.text: Nexora Connect plugs in a broad catalogue of services: mail, calendar, customer relations, storage, billing. Each connection belongs to a workspace and is qualified service by service.

cards.title: An OpenAI-format API.
cards.text: An API (the door through which other software calls a service) gives access to models and published agents, in the OpenAI format that many tools already understand: keys, quotas, consumption metering.

cards.title: Your website.
cards.text: A published agent shows up on your site with one line of code (chat bubble, frame or link). WorkStudio also installs as an application from a compatible browser.

cards.title: An internal Assistant.
cards.text: A chat where your teams talk to the company's published agents, with their history and attached files.

cards.title: Agents that help each other.
cards.text: An agent can hand a request to another published agent, with limited depth and no loops.

cards.title: A simple installation.
cards.text: One command on a Docker server (a tool that packages software), on Linux or macOS, then backup, restore and update commands.

translation.title: The limits, stated plainly.
translation.body: A product is also judged by what it writes about its limits. Here are ours, as of this page's date.

items.title: Verified here, not yet at a customer.
items.text: WorkStudio has been verified on Nexora's test server with several models hosted elsewhere than on that server. No customer result is announced.

items.title: Tool-using agents need a capable model.
items.text: A small local model is not always enough for agents that call tools. The model is chosen with the case.

items.title: Two options are off the beaten path.
items.text: The code interpreter is off by default and can only be turned on by an administrator. Web search sends its queries outside the instance: it is available only if an administrator turns it on.

items.title: Starter templates are general.
items.text: They do not follow Quebec tax rules: taxes, formats and vocabulary are adapted to your business.

items.title: Connections are qualified.
items.text: Some services require an administrator to first register an application with the provider, and a public HTTPS address for the instance.

items.question: Can we try it with no commitment?
items.answer: There is no account to create for now: self-service offers are not open yet. We offer a demonstration, on fictional data, then we talk about your case.

items.question: Do I need to know how to code?
items.answer: Not for everyday use: a workflow reads as cards, is set up through forms and is tested step by step. Special cases may need code; we handle that with you.

items.question: Does my data leave my server?
items.answer: By default, indexing of your documents is computed on the instance's server. An external model is never configured without your written agreement, and each model shows where it runs.

items.question: Can it integrate with our tools?
items.answer: Yes, through connectors, an OpenAI-format API, or by displaying an agent on your website. Each connection is qualified.

items.question: How long to install?
items.answer: Installation is one command on a Docker server; putting a case into service depends on your situation, with no universal timeline.

translation.title: See WorkStudio at work.
translation.text: We prepare a demonstration on fictional data, then we talk about your first case.
